Data

Load the data

The data are a dataframe with columns for brood year (brood_year), number of spawners (spawners), number of recruits (recruits) and PDO at year \(t-2\) in summer (pdo_summer_t2) and in winter (pdo_winter_t2).

The timeseries ranges from 1952 to 2005.

General tasks

Use the information and data in the previous section to answer the following questions. Note that if any model is not converging, then you will need to increase the maxit parameter in the control argument/list that gets passed to MARSS(). For example, you might try control=list(maxit=2000).

  1. Begin by fitting a reduced form of Ricker’s model that includes only a time-varying level (\(\alpha_t\)) and observation error (\(v_t\)). That is,

\[\begin{align*} \text{log}(R_t) &= \alpha_t + \text{log}(S_t) + v_t \\ \text{log}(R_t/S_t) &= \alpha_t + v_t \end{align*}\]

This model assumes no density-dependent survival in that the number of recruits is an ascending function of spawners. Plot the ts of \(\alpha_t\) and note the AICc for this model. Also plot appropriate model diagnostics.

  1. Fit the expanded model that includes the winter PDO index as the covariate (pdo_winter_t2). What is the mean level of productivity? Plot the ts of \(\delta_t\) and note the AICc for this model. Also plot appropriate model diagnostics.

  2. Based on AICc, which of the models above is the most parsimonious? Is it well behaved (i.e., are the model assumptions met)? Plot the model forecasts for the best model. Is this a good forecast model?

  3. Consider other environmental factors that could influence the time-varying intrinsic productivity of these salmon. For example, are there other large-scale indices of ocean conditions (e.g., sea-surface temperature, El Niño Southern Oscillation)? You could also consider the possible influence of other salmon stocks such as those we examined in Lab 1.

Methods

General model structure

Base Model structure

We began by fitting a reduced form of Ricker’s model that includes only a time-varying level (\(\alpha_t\)) and observation error (\(v_t\)). That is,

\[ \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right) = \alpha_t + v_t \]

\[\begin{align*} \text{Observation:} \quad & y_t = Z x_t + v_t \\ & y_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_t + v_t, \quad v_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R) \\[1em] \text{State:} \quad & x_t = B x_{t-1} + w_t \\ & \alpha_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_{t-1} + w_t, \quad w_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q) \end{align*}\]

This model assumes no density-dependent survival in that the number of recruits is an ascending function of spawners. We did not include any environmental variables for this step.

# Assuming you have logRS = log(R/S) as a time series
logRS <-  log(SR_data$spawners)/log(SR_data$recruits) 


model.list1 <- list(
  Z = matrix(1),
  A = matrix(0),
  R = "diagonal and equal",
  B = matrix(1),
  U = matrix(0),
  Q = "unconstrained",
  x0 = "unconstrained",
  tinitx = 0
)

fit1 <- MARSS(logRS, model = model.list1)
## Success! abstol and log-log tests passed at 21 iterations.
## Alert: conv.test.slope.tol is 0.5.
## Test with smaller values (<0.1) to ensure convergence.
## 
## MARSS fit is
## Estimation method: kem 
## Convergence test: conv.test.slope.tol = 0.5, abstol = 0.001
## Estimation converged in 21 iterations. 
## Log-likelihood: 37.88274 
## AIC: -69.76548   AICc: -69.1501   
##  
##       Estimate
## R.R    0.00303
## Q.Q    0.00498
## x0.x0  0.90376
## Initial states (x0) defined at t=0
## 
## Standard errors have not been calculated. 
## Use MARSSparamCIs to compute CIs and bias estimates.
# Extract time-varying alpha_t
alpha_t1 <- fit1$states[1, ]

Plot the ts of \(\alpha_t\) and note the AICc for this model. Also plot appropriate model diagnostics.

# Plot time series
ts.plot(alpha_t1, main = "Time-varying Intercept (alpha_t) - Reduced Model", ylab = "alpha_t")

# AICc
cat("AICc of Reduced Model: ", fit1$AICc, "\n")
## AICc of Reduced Model:  -69.1501
#Vector to store the AICcs of all models
mod_compare <- rep(0, 4)
mod_compare[1] <- fit1$AICc

# Diagnostics (Residuals, QQ Plot and ACF)
plot(residuals(fit1))

Full Model Structure

Next,we fitted the full Ricker model with a time-varying intercept and a static effect of spawners.

For this model, we need the time series of \(\alpha_t\), which is an estimate of the stock productivity in the absence of density-dependent effects.

The equation for this model is now:

\[ \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right) = \alpha_t - \beta S_t + v_t \]

\[\begin{align*} \text{Observation:} \quad & y_t = Z x_t + C c_t + v_t \\ & y_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_t + (-1) \cdot S_t + v_t, \quad v_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R) \\[1em] \text{State:} \quad & x_t = B x_{t-1} + w_t \\ & \alpha_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_{t-1} + w_t, \quad w_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, Q) \end{align*}\]

This means that \(\alpha_t\) is time-varying and \(\beta_t\) is static.

# Checking this because of failure
y <- matrix(logRS, nrow = 1)

# Make the covariate matrix
covars <- matrix(SR_data$spawners, nrow = 1)


# MARSS model list
model.list2 <- list(
  Z = matrix(1),         # observation matrix (1 state)
  A = matrix(0),         # no intercept
  R = matrix("r"),       # observation error variance
  B = matrix(1),         # state dynamics: alpha_t = alpha_{t-1} + w_t
  U = matrix(0),         # no drift
  Q = matrix("q"),       # process error variance for alpha_t
  x0 = matrix("mu"),     # initial state mean
  tinitx = 0,
  C = matrix(-1),        # static beta coefficient for S_t
  c = covars
)

Addition of covariates

We fitted the expanded model that includes the summer PDO index as the covariate (pdo_summer_t2).

The equation for this model is now:

\[ \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right) = \alpha_t - \beta S_t + \delta \cdot \text{PDO}_t + v_t \]

\[\begin{align*} \text{Observation:} \quad & y_t = Z \alpha_t + C_1 c_{1t} + C_2 c_{2t} + v_t \\ & y_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_t + (-1) \cdot S_t + \delta \cdot \text{PDO}_t + v_t, \quad v_t \sim \text{N}(0, R) \\[1em] \text{State:} \quad & \alpha_t = B \alpha_{t-1} + w_t \\ & \alpha_t = 1 \cdot \alpha_{t-1} + w_t, \quad w_t \sim \text{N}(0, Q) \end{align*}\]

What is the mean level of productivity? Plot the ts of \(\delta_t\) and note the AICc for this model. Also plot appropriate model diagnostics.

# Combine covariates: Spawner and PDO
covars_PS <- rbind(SR_data$spawners, SR_data$pdo_summer_t2)

model.list3 <- list(
  Z = matrix(1),
  A = matrix(0),
  R = "diagonal and equal",
  B = matrix(1),
  U = matrix(0),
  Q = "unconstrained",
  x0 = "unconstrained",
  tinitx = 0,
  C = matrix(c(-1, "delta")),   # Static beta, time-varying delta
  c = covars_PS
)

fit3 <- MARSS(logRS, model = model.list3)
## Success! abstol and log-log tests passed at 24 iterations.
## Alert: conv.test.slope.tol is 0.5.
## Test with smaller values (<0.1) to ensure convergence.

## Estimation converged in 24 iterations. 
## Log-likelihood: 38.61185 
## AIC: -67.22371   AICc: -65.60209   
##  
##          Estimate
## R.R      2.74e-03
## Q.Q      5.07e-03
## x0.x0    8.73e-01
## C.-1     1.01e-06
## C.delta -1.35e-02
## Initial states (x0) defined at t=0
## 
## Standard errors have not been calculated. 
## Use MARSSparamCIs to compute CIs and bias estimates.
alpha_t3 <- fit3$states[1, ]
delta_t <- fit3$par$C[2, ]

ts.plot(alpha_t3, main = "Time-varying Intercept (alpha_t) - With PDO", ylab = "alpha_t")

cat("AICc of PDO Model: ", fit3$AICc, "\n")
## AICc of PDO Model:  -65.60209
mod_compare[3] <- fit3$AICc

# Plot of delta (effect of PDO)
#plot(pdo_summer_t2, delta_t, type = "b", main = "Effect of Summer PDO (delta_t)", ylab = "delta_t")

covars_PW <- rbind(SR_data$spawners, SR_data$pdo_winter_t2)

model.list3 <- list(

  Q = "unconstrained",
  x0 = "unconstrained",

fit4 <- MARSS(logRS, model = model.list3)

Resulting Model forms (matrix form)

Model 1: Reduced Ricker Model (time-varying productivity only)

\[ \boxed{ \begin{cases} \mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{v}_t \\ \mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{B} \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \mathbf{w}_t \end{cases} } \]

where

\[ \mathbf{y}_t = \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right), \quad \mathbf{x}_t = \alpha_t \]

and matrices/vectors:

\[ \mathbf{Z} = [1], \quad \mathbf{B} = [1], \quad \mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, R), \quad \mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, Q) \]

Model 2: Full Ricker with static spawner effect

\[ \boxed{ \begin{cases} \mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{C} \mathbf{c}_t + \mathbf{v}_t \\ \mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{B} \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \mathbf{w}_t \end{cases} } \]

where

\[ \mathbf{y}_t = \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right), \quad \mathbf{x}_t = \alpha_t, \quad \mathbf{c}_t = S_t \]

and matrices/vectors:

\[ \mathbf{Z} = [1], \quad \mathbf{C} = [-1], \quad \mathbf{B} = [1], \quad \mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, R), \quad \mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, Q) \]

Model 3: Expanded Ricker with PDO covariate

\[ \boxed{ \begin{cases} \mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{Z} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{C} \mathbf{c}_t + \mathbf{v}_t \\ \mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{B} \mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \mathbf{w}_t \end{cases} } \]

where

\[ \mathbf{y}_t = \log\left(\frac{R_t}{S_t}\right), \quad \mathbf{x}_t = \alpha_t, \quad \mathbf{c}_t = \begin{bmatrix} S_t \\ \text{PDO}_t \end{bmatrix} \]

and matrices/vectors:

\[ \mathbf{Z} = [1], \quad \mathbf{C} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & \delta \end{bmatrix}, \quad \mathbf{B} = [1], \quad \mathbf{v}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, R), \quad \mathbf{w}_t \sim \mathbf{N}(0, Q) \]

Discussion

Consider other environmental factors that could influence the time-varying intrinsic productivity of these salmon.
